title: The Heart and Mind of Editing Award-Winning Music Videos
note: Placeholder transcript for the AI Week demo, not a real transcription. Replace via generate_transcripts.py once ffmpeg + an OpenAI/Whisper key are available.

segments.text: The editor opens on 'cutting to intention' - starting every music video edit from the emotional beat of the track rather than the raw footage, and letting pacing follow the music's own rhythm.
A breakdown of beat-matching cuts: finding the musical accents in a track first, then building the edit's rhythm around them before touching performance footage.
Color grading for mood - how a warmer, lower-contrast grade versus a cold, high-contrast one changes the emotional read of the exact same performance footage.
Working with a director's vision: translating a director's reference boards and mood language into actual timeline decisions without losing their intent.
Project organization in Premiere for music video work - bin structure, multicam syncing to the master audio track, and labeling conventions that scale to hundreds of takes.
Sound design tricks beyond the master track: layering subtle whooshes and impacts under cuts to make edits feel more physical, even in a purely visual medium.
On burnout: the editor describes hitting a wall mid-career, and the specific changes to workload and feedback loops with artists/labels that helped them recover.
Closing thoughts on redefining success as an editor - moving away from view counts as the only measure, toward whether the edit served the song and the artist's intent.
